target: tracker.sh supersede — a commit-ish on the default branch satisfies the dependency
cmd:
mkdir -p factory/specs; printf -- '---
id: 001
title: dependent
status: specd
depends_on: 002
---
body
' > factory/specs/001-a.md; printf -- '---
id: 002
title: dep
status: built
---
body
' > factory/specs/002-b.md; git init -q .; git add -A; git -c user.email=t@test -c user.name=test commit -qm 'the hotfix'; SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"; source "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh"; tracker_supersede factory/specs/002-b.md me "$SHA" 'landed by hand' >/dev/null 2>&1; UNMET="$(_tracker_unmet factory/specs/001-a.md)"; if CLAIMED=$(tracker_claim specd building loop 2>/dev/null); then EC=0; else EC=$?; fi; jq -n --argjson ec "$EC" --arg unmet "$UNMET" --arg s1 "$(_tracker_field factory/specs/001-a.md status)" '{ec: $ec, unmet: $unmet, s1: $s1}'
_note: the user's actual case: work landed by hand outside the factory, so the spec is irrelevant but its dependents are genuinely unblocked. Verification is real git ancestry, not a trusted flag — delete the `git init` line from this setup and it degrades to 064's behavior, which is the mutation test for the check.
